free_tier.stated: no free GPU tier is published; the live rate card read on 2026-11-03 lists 19 GPU types from USD 0.36 an hour: H100 80GB USD 3.86, A100 80GB USD 1.73, L40S 48GB USD 0.54, L40 USD 0.47, RTX 4090 USD 0.57, H200 USD 4.63, B200 USD 7.67. No L4 is listed. Billed by the second on most GPUs and by the minute on a few; booting is never billed.
free_tier.notes: prepaid terms of 1 to 12 months are up to 15% off; the aggregator shows H100 SXM at USD 2.49 where the provider rate card shows USD 3.86

per_object_cap.notes: storage volumes of 10 GB to 10,000 GB at USD 0.03 per GB a month are a separate line

retention.notes: credits do not expire; storage volumes are kept when the instance is deleted

egress.terms: not published on the pages read

interface_detail: taken from the pricing page, which lists SSH, a CLI and an unauthenticated /api/gpu-pricing endpoint; not probed
tooling: SSH, Jupyter and VS Code in the browser, Python and TypeScript SDKs, a CLI and an MCP server; an OpenAI-compatible inference API on the same balance
chaining: One prepaid balance pays for GPU hours, token-billed inference and storage volumes; the public /api/gpu-pricing endpoint publishes the live rate card without a key.

limits.value: a launch needs USD 10 or an hour of the machine, whichever is more; a balance is added by card from USD 20

limits_note: A launch is gated on a prepaid balance added by card; there is no free allowance.
binding_note: A launch is gated on a prepaid balance added by card; there is no free allowance.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form asks for name, email, password and an age or consent checkbox; balance is added by card before use, from USD 20 to USD 10,000 at a time. Reserved multi-node clusters need a verification of the company and the need. No phone or ID document is stated for self-serve.

reliability_note: Capacity is sourced multi-cloud rather than from owned data centres per the aggregator profile; sold-out GPUs stay listed for 30 days at 0 available per the rate card.
